project: Anuvritti - V0 complete, V1 Make It Magical, reshaped 2026-08-26
scope_note: V0 (Phases 1-4) is complete and hardened: PRD 48 features 1-9, PRD 49 exclusions enforced as tests. V1 (Phases 5-9) is PRD 50 'Make It Magical'. Decisions taken 2026-08-25: native iOS and Android together via Expo, because the design tokens are then TypeScript and CSS and the same visual language renders both the app and the film's Chromium scenes; the Surface first, with Voice and the Memory Compiler to follow immediately after rather than eventually; and the rendering core extracted from autovideo-engine into a shared filmkit package rather than vendored or called across a file contract. Expanded 2026-08-26 from a V1 feature plan into a production programme: Phases 10-14 carry the work between 'it demonstrates' and 'a family can rely on it for eighteen years' - the app in a pocket, the machine that runs it, the render farm, the long now, and a product a family can actually have. The ordering is a dependency graph, not a schedule; there are no dates because the constraint is correctness, not calendar. Reshaped 2026-08-26 after a four-way review (Phase 7 audit, PRD gap analysis, app critique, adversarial roadmap review): Phase 7 gains the floor the product stood on in words only - a renderer that draws a pixel, a phone that is actually wired, CI that passes on the next push. Phase 8 becomes 'Make It Magical' and carries the PRD promises no task held: Future Inbox, Papa Today's presence prompts, the Annual Interview in the child's own voice, sealed capsules, the child's first screen. Phase 9 becomes 'Real': a server that is not the laptop, a restored backup, the app on the founder's phone, and PRD 54 run for thirty days. Phases 10 to 14 now depend on TASK-910, the dated answer to that month, because PRD 64 says not to start by building the platform, and the tracker had.

tasks.description: Project scaffold and toolchain: pyproject.toml (src layout, py3.12), pytest+coverage config, ruff, mypy strict, requirements.txt/-dev, Makefile.
Shared kernel: Result/Ok/Err (Either), DomainError code catalog matching docs/contracts/errors.md, typed identifiers, Clock and IdGenerator ports.
12-factor Settings loaded from env only (zero secrets in repo) plus structured JSON logging with request correlation and PII-safe fields.
Executable architecture fitness function: assert domain imports stdlib only and the dependency rule (interfaces -> application -> domain) is never violated.

Harden scripts/orchestrate.sh: fix the phase-name word-splitting bug (jq output iterated unquoted), add tracker.json schema validation, dependency-gate tasks so a task cannot start before its dependencies are completed, and record changed files per task.

Domain value objects: IntentType (six V0 intents gated via v0_set), SparkStatus, SourceKind, Visibility, MemberRole, AgeRange, Confidence, SourceRef, and Attributed[T] carrying value/source/confidence/human_override.
Family aggregate: Family, Member, ChildProfile with age computation, role-based permission checks and visibility rules (owner vs subject separation per child data rights).

Spark aggregate: capture, apply_inference with provenance, record_why, override_field, mark_suggested, snooze, archive, plan, experience. Full lifecycle state machine returning Err(InvalidTransition) - never raising. Emits domain events.
Remaining entities: Moment (Spark -> lived life, all evidence optional), LittleThing, RightNowSnapshot, MediaObject.

Application ports: SparkRepository, MomentRepository, FamilyRepository, LittleThingRepository, RightNowRepository, MediaStore, IntentEngine, Transcriber, EventPublisher, UnitOfWork - all Result-typed Protocols.

Return Engine domain service: pure weighted scoring (age_fit, maturation, occasion_fit, intent_actionability, why_present, novelty) plus constitutional dampers (snooze cooldown, archived exclusion, daily cap, no-guilt reason text).
HeuristicIntentEngine adapter: deterministic, offline, lexicon-driven inference of intent/category/age_range/tags/title with calibrated confidence. No network call.
Capture use cases: CaptureSpark (universal capture, inline enrichment, under-10s no-form path), RecordWhy, OverrideAiField.

Safe Vault search use case: keyword + facet retrieval answering the PRD example queries (toys I saved, things for age 3, funny things, things about space, things to do outside, things I wanted to teach him). No folders.
Return use cases: GetWorthBringingBack (scores, caps, marks suggested, builds guilt-free reason) and RespondToSuggestion (maybe_later | lets_do_it | not_relevant_anymore).
MarkAsDone use case: Spark -> Moment with every attachment optional (nothing is a valid answer), emitting MomentCreated with days_from_capture for the Intent->Moment metric.
Presence use cases: CaptureLittleThing (one tap, no structure) and Right Now prompt selection + CaptureRightNow snapshot.
SQLite persistence: idempotent migrations, WAL, UnitOfWork, and repositories for family/spark/moment/little_thing/right_now/media/domain_event. Provenance stored as discrete columns, never a blob.
EncryptedFilesystemMediaStore: content-addressed, Fernet encryption at rest with key from env, MIME allow-list, size cap, and byte-level delete.
Family data rights use cases: ExportEverything (complete readable archive + media manifest) and DeleteEverything (hard delete including media bytes), both emitting audit events.
FastAPI interface adapter implementing docs/contracts/openapi.yaml, DomainError->HTTP mapping per the error catalog, and the composition root wiring all adapters.

E2E golden path: capture a reel -> AI infers -> why recorded -> months pass (frozen clock) -> Worth Bringing Back surfaces it -> lets_do_it -> mark done -> Moment exists and Intent->Moment metric increments.

Ethical Constitution as executable tests: no guilt/urgency vocabulary in suggestions, no streaks/scores/leaderboards on the wire, daily suggestion cap honoured, no location or screen-monitoring field accepted anywhere, PRD 49 non-scope absent from the codebase.
Resilience and edge cases: link-rot (external source disappears, Spark keeps meaning), idempotent capture, clock boundaries, empty/oversized media, unicode, concurrent writes.
Coverage gate: enforce >=90% on domain+application and >=80% overall in pytest config, so CI fails below threshold.
Observability: /health, /ready, /metrics (Prometheus text incl. anti-metrics), request-id middleware, JSON access logs with no PII bodies.
Container: multi-stage Dockerfile on slim base, non-root user, no build toolchain in final layer, healthcheck, .dockerignore.
GitHub Actions CI: ruff, mypy strict, pytest with coverage gates, pip-audit, secret scan, docker build - all blocking.
Hardening report (docs/HARDENING.md), operator runbook and README covering run/test/export/delete and the 30-day validation protocol.
Preserve autovideo-engine before it is refactored: 4,779 lines and 13 test files currently have zero commits. Run its suite, then initialise history. Requires explicit user consent to commit.

packages/world - the Anuvritti design language as code. Colour, type, space, elevation and motion tokens exported as both TypeScript and CSS custom properties, so one visual language serves the native app and the film scenes.
world specimen: a living page rendering every token and primitive, so drift between app and film is visible rather than discovered.

tests/design - constitution tests for the interface, the pixel equivalent of test_no_guilt.py: no badges, counts, streaks or red dots; urgency colour reserved for destructive actions; elapsed time never rendered as a number.
Expo application for iOS and Android, with a typed API client generated from the existing docs/contracts/openapi.yaml so the wire contract stays single-sourced.
tasks.notes: packages/client: a Python generator emits the typed surface from docs/contracts/openapi.yaml (22 operations, 32 schemas) plus a hand-written zero-dependency runtime - transport, Result envelope, session, queue. Generated output is committed and tests/design/test_generated_client.py fails on drift. tests/integration/test_contract_conformance.py compares the contract to the routed application both ways and found GET /media/{media_id} and GET /families/{family_id} undocumented on its first run.

tasks.description: The Spark as an object rather than a card: front is what was saved, back is why it was saved. The flip is the product's core gesture.
tasks.notes: apps/anuvritti/src/components/Spark.tsx. Front is what was saved, back is why. The flip is the only motion allowed past the design system's ceiling, and it is announced to a screen reader because a rotation is not an event one can observe.

tasks.description: Time as language, never as a number: bind describe_elapsed semantics through the client so the interface can say 'a Tuesday last spring' and cannot say '247 days'.
tasks.notes: days_since_capture removed from the wire; Spark.saved and Suggestion.elapsed carry the phrase. Instant and Elapsed are branded in the generated client, and packages/client contains no Date.parse, new Date, Date.now, getTime or valueOf - asserted by a test that also mutation-checks its own regexes.

tasks.description: Capture under ten seconds: an iOS Share Extension and an Android SEND intent filter that post straight to /v1/sparks and answer with 'Saved.' - the PRD's primary path, native on both platforms.
tasks.notes: expo-sharing's first-party config plugin (verified against the published 57.0.15 tarball) covers iOS share extension and Android SEND in one declaration. readShare() is a pure function with no expo import and 20 tests.

tasks.description: Offline-first capture queue with idempotent replay, so a parent with no signal still saves in under ten seconds.
tasks.notes: Idempotency-Key on all four capture endpoints, storing a request fingerprint so a reused key with a different body is a CONFLICT rather than a silent success. Client queue enqueues without touching the network, classifies failure rather than counting it, and jitters its backoff.

tasks.description: One-tap correction: the inferred chip cycles through alternatives and never becomes a form, driving the Attributed override path the domain already models.
tasks.notes: The chip cycles through a likelihood-ordered permutation of the six intents; every cycle is proven to visit all six and return. Optimistic, so the word changes before the server answers.

tasks.description: Device pairing authentication - closes HARDENING 5.1 for one family without taking on full multi-tenancy.
tasks.notes: Bearer device tokens; the token is the family. Bootstrap pairs the founding device in the same call that creates the family. Codes are 8 Crockford characters, single use, ten minutes, five global attempts. Only SHA-256 fingerprints are stored. Every failure mode answers identically. 52 integration tests.

tasks.description: Worth Bringing Back on the phone: at most one suggestion, dismissible forever, no counter and no unread state.
tasks.notes: whatToBringBack returns one or nothing, and its type has no field a count could be built from.

tasks.description: On-device end to end: share, saved, returned months later, lived. The golden path from tests/e2e, on real hardware.
tasks.notes: tests/e2e/test_the_app_against_the_server.py runs the real generated TypeScript client against the real ASGI application over a real socket, with the server's clock advanced eight months mid-story. docs/DEVICE.md is the four-item checklist for what genuinely needs hardware.
tasks.note: Closed 2026-08-28. The reopen found three things and the work found three more. The route graph: app/pair.tsx was unreachable - no link, redirect or declared screen pointed at it - so a phone with no token opened Today, took two 401s and said "Nothing today. That's normal." to a stranger. Now Stack.Protected guards two groups on src/model/threshold.ts, pairing exits by ceasing to exist, a 401 signs the device out (a 403 does not) and the sign-out clears the credential and never the queue. npm install had never succeeded: expo-router@~7.0.0 does not exist and three @expo-google-fonts pins were above the published version, so every dependency is now Expo SDK 57's own bundledNativeModules.json. The repository had no TypeScript gate at all - `node --test` strips types without checking them - so `make types-ts` now compiles four projects and found a real return of undefined in nextIntent, a readonly array being pushed to in the capture queue, a World.shadow type that excluded the dark theme, and a font named by world.font.mono that useFonts was never given (the pairing code rendered proportional, where O/0 and I/1 are the confusions Crockford exists to prevent). test/threshold.test.ts walks app/ and fails on any orphaned route, so TASK-715 and TASK-716 inherit the check. docs/DEVICE.md is shorter by what became software. What still needs hardware stays with TASK-907.

tasks.description: Hold to talk with a live waveform; release saves. Five seconds is the target, not a minimum.
The recording is the artifact and the transcript is only an index: voice always renders above text and text never replaces it.
Transcriber port and an on-device adapter that makes no network call, so PRD 44's no-public-model default stays absolute rather than configured.
Voice to intent: transcripts feed the existing heuristic engine so speaking earns the same free categorisation that typing does.
Little Things and the seed of the Papa Voice Vault - and the reason to record: every clip becomes a line in this year's film.
Constitution test: no recording is ever rejected, trimmed or re-recorded for being unpolished. Preserve imperfection.

phases.name: Phase 7: The Memory Compiler
phases.owner: Principal Systems Architect / Senior Staff Backend Engineer

tasks.description: Extract filmkit: narration, timing, timeline, captions, compositor, cache store, browser rendering and manifest lifted out of autovideo-engine into a standalone package with no knowledge of either product.
tasks.notes: filmkit 0.1.0: 9 modules, 1863 lines. The three heavy dependencies are ports - Painter (browser), Synthesiser (voice), Runner (shell) - so importing filmkit requires nothing installed. Workspace is injected; no environment variable is read anywhere.

tasks.description: autovideo-engine consumes filmkit and its existing test files pass unchanged - the proof that the extraction was faithful rather than a rewrite.
tasks.notes: 1091 lines deleted from autovideo/src, 393 added. Not one test file touched: 97 tests pass unchanged. Docker build context moved to the parent so filmkit can be copied in - NOT verified by a real image build.

tasks.description: filmkit inherits this project's gates: ruff, mypy strict, coverage at or above ninety per cent.
tasks.notes: 207 tests, 97.40% coverage, ruff and mypy --strict clean. tests/test_knows_no_product.py fails the build on a product name, an environment read, or a top-level browser import.

tasks.description: FilmCompiler port and a FilmkitFilmCompiler adapter, keeping Chromium and FFmpeg outside the domain and off the family's box.
tasks.notes: FilmCompiler declares one method, compile(spec) -> CompiledFilm. There is no render, no output path and no codec on the protocol, so a video cannot be asked for through it. FilmkitFilmCompiler imports only filmkit's weightless half - narration, timing, timeline, captions - and a test enforces that whitelist, checks the composition root never reaches anuvritti.adapters.film, and proves both checks can fail. filmkit is an optional extra, absent from requirements.txt, so the production image never grows it. CompiledScene refuses to hold audio longer than its picture; a capped scene that would need trimming fails the compile with FILM_NOT_COMPILABLE instead. 36 tests, 100% coverage on both new modules; make check green (1715 python tests, 96.79%).

tasks.description: Moments compile to a filmspec plus a bundle of real media, with every scene declaring the source ids it draws from.
tasks.notes: ComposeFilmUseCase turns a family's Moments into a FilmSpec plus a MediaBundle. Every scene is built from a Moment and the Spark it came from and cites both by id, plus any photograph and recording; SceneKind.is_evidence makes that structural - FilmScene refuses to hold a MOMENT/VOICE/SPARK/LITTLE_THING scene with an empty cites, so an invented scene cannot be constructed, only title cards cite nothing. FilmDraft holds spec and bundle and refuses to exist unless they agree exactly in both directions: nothing missing (a film with a hole) and nothing spare (a child's recording that left the house for no reason). A Moment with audio but no measured VoiceNote fails the composition naming the moment rather than compiling a silent scene, and only a human transcript becomes a caption - a machine reading is an index, not a quotation. CompileFilmUseCase joins this to TASK-704's port and returns a FilmPackage, never a video. 43 integration tests over real SQLite + the encrypted media store + the real filmkit compiler, 3 more failure paths, 100% on application/film.py; make check green (1765 python tests, 97%).

tasks.description: Provenance checkpoints: a frame that cannot cite a real Spark, Moment or media id fails the build, and provenance.json ships beside the film. autovideo's evidence rule, applied to a family's memory.
tasks.notes: VerifyProvenanceUseCase follows every citation in a FilmDraft back to the archive and returns a Provenance ledger - one entry per citation, VERIFIED / MISSING / ALTERED. It is built as though the spec came from a stranger: media and voice-note citations are checked against the bytes (re-hashed on read), never against the catalogue row the composer already trusted. A repository that fails to answer propagates rather than being recorded as MISSING; a cross-family citation gets the same wording an unknown id gets. FilmPackage now requires the ledger and refuses to be constructed if it is incomplete, if it vouches for something the film does not cite, or if anything failed - so an unverified film cannot exist as a value. CompileFilmUseCase verifies before the compiler is ever called. FilesystemFilmExporter writes film.json, provenance.json and media/ into a 0700 folder, refusing a non-empty directory and re-hashing every file on the way out. Gates: 16 constitution tests, 12 verifier unit tests, 6 exporter unit tests, 100% on domain/film.py, application/film.py and adapters/film/export.py, 99% on application/provenance.py; make check green (1809 python tests, 97%, ruff + mypy strict, 94 npm tests).

tasks.description: Narration is the parent's own recorded voice, measured never estimated. Synthesis is permitted only for neutral connective tissue and is marked as synthetic wherever it appears.
tasks.notes: ConnectiveLine is the entire vocabulary a synthesiser may speak: four fixed sentences in the domain, containing no name, date or placeholder. SceneVoice refuses a synthetic voice that says anything else, that carries no file (a file is where the measurement comes from), or that a non-machine origin claims; FilmScene refuses any synthetic voice over a scene that cites, so 'synthesis is connective tissue only' is checked where scenes are built. The Narrator port takes a ConnectiveLine rather than a string, so there is no parameter anywhere through which a sentence about a child could reach a synthesiser, and it returns a probed length. ComposeFilmUseCase takes an optional narrator defaulting to None - the shipped product opens in silence - and a synthesis failure becomes silence, never an estimate. Every synthetic line is marked in SceneVoice.caption (which is what the timeline and therefore the captions are cut from), in CompiledFilm.narration, and in the film.json that ships beside provenance.json. 21 constitution tests; the Archive harness was extracted to tests/support so both film constitutions describe the same family.

tasks.description: Film scenes built from packages/world, so the film looks like the app because it is literally the same tokens.
tasks.notes: Film scenes are HTML documents linking the same dist/world.css the app is drawn from; scenes.css adds only layout and names no colour, font or size of its own. Type scales by moving the film's root size so the app's ratios are preserved; spacing stays on the px scale. check-scenes.ts reads the Python domain and fails if a SceneKind has no layout, if the frame size or fps drift from _FRAME_WIDTH/_FRAME_HEIGHT/_FPS, if a scene hard-codes a value, if a custom property is not declared in world.css, if anything animates (a screenshot of a moving page is non-deterministic), if an external host appears, if a caption is not passed through verbatim including the machine mark, or if the compiler stops labelling timeline scenes with their kind. The film commits to data-theme=light rather than inheriting a headless browser's preference; images use contain rather than cover; a scene with no picture renders no img. 15 unit tests plus the gate; the gate was verified to fail on injected drift.

tasks.description: The Year: one film per child per year, the window derived from the child's birthday, every scene a real Moment, Spark, Little Thing or recording, opening and closing cards only. Compiled from the founder's own month via TASK-712, so 'That's in this year's film' is a statement. Interview, capsules and a second voice are TASK-810 and TASK-813.

A teaser render from seeded real media (a dozen photographs and recordings in the workspace, never committed), so the destination is visible long before there is a year of material. `make teaser` renders it; the gate is ffprobe agreeing with the compiled timeline, not a file existing.

Commit Phase 7 and unbreak CI: requirements-dev.txt ends in `../filmkit`, so the next push fails at pip install. Decide filmkit's home (fold into packages/filmkit in this monorepo, or pin `filmkit @ git+...@<sha>`), install it editable, add the three npm suites to ci.yml, and push all three repositories somewhere that is not this laptop.

FilmRenderer: the first pixel. A port and a ChromiumFfmpegRenderer adapter that turns a FilmExport folder into an mp4: each scene to HTML via packages/world/scenes with world.css, scenes.css and the photograph inlined (Chromium's set_content has no base URL), fonts bundled so a frame is the same offline, one PNG per scene via filmkit.browser, silence generated for silent scenes, per-scene render and concat via filmkit.compositor. `make film ARCHIVE=<dir>`.

The phone, wired: install dependencies and commit a lockfile (`expo install --fix`, tsc clean); a pairing gate in _layout so an unpaired phone reaches /pair and `router.replace('/')` after; image shares uploaded and captured instead of dropped on the floor (provider.tsx:104); playback authenticated via `{uri, headers}` on useAudioPlayer; HoldToTalk's arm cancelled when the finger lifts during the permission sheet; voice uploads spooled so a recording is never orphaned.

tasks.description: tests/design reads the app: saffron appears only in the waveform and the voice player (today the 'Saved.' tile wears it); no `\d+ days` string; no hardcoded pronoun or relationship in copy; every screen's strings routed through one said.ts. Mutation-checked like the Python scanners.

The threshold: first run ends with the child's name, not a tour. Family name, then 'And who is this for?' (display name and birthday, POST /families/{id}/children), then the first share. A pairing sheet that shows the eight characters in mono at year size and nothing else, for as long as it is good. No step count, no progress, and the child's age never rendered as a number.

This Year's Film, on the phone: a route linked from the vault's kept line and the bottom of Today, titled with the child's name and the year in the display face, showing every recording and every Spark with a why in capture order, months as the only structure, and one sentence: 'This is what the film is made of.' A compile route in openapi.yaml and the client; the rendered film plays here once TASK-712 has made it. No count of scenes, no minutes, no percentage, no 'keep going'.

Measured on the server, never trusted from the handset: VoiceNote.duration_seconds is probed from the bytes (filmkit.narration.measure via ffprobe) at keep time, and the handset's figure is only compared. A clip the client under-reports can no longer pass the 'would be cut off' invariant.

Record the render toolchain in a portable artifact manifest beside the MP4: Playwright and Chromium revisions, FFmpeg version, exact encoder arguments, frame hashes, and scene-to-frame mapping, so a film can explain exactly how its pixels were made years later.

phases.name: Phase 8: Make It Magical
phases.owner: Design Lead / Senior Staff Backend Engineer / Senior Staff Mobile Engineer

tasks.description: FamilyLexicon: every correction trains that one family's private lexicon, held in the family's own archive. No shared model, no network, no other family's data.
tasks.note: Closed 2026-08-28. FamilyLexicon is a per-family term tally with five refusals made structural: no merge/union/combine exists in the module (an AST test reads the source and fails if one appears); only a human override can build a Correction, so the engine cannot train on its own guesses; one correction counts but does not speak, because a product that reorganises itself around a single tap feels haunted; a word this family uses two ways teaches nothing rather than siding with the higher count; and it holds counts with no SparkId, ChildId or MemberId anywhere, so a leaked lexicon says only that this family says 'sanskaar' and means TEACH. schema v4 adds lexicon_term keyed (family_id, field, term, means). The seam is real end to end: OverrideFieldUseCase learns inside the same transaction as the save (a lexicon updated for a correction that rolled back would record things nobody said) and swallows its own failures, because answering a parent's correction with an error about the learning would make the correction look rejected. CaptureSparkUseCase reads the lexicon and treats an unreadable one as absent - a share must never fail because of a family's own vocabulary. It rides the export and dies with the family, both directions of PRD 44. 32 domain tests, 11 integration, 100% coverage.

tasks.description: The unsorted pile is a first-class state: an uncategorised Spark still returns, on time alone, and is never counted or nagged about.

Future Inbox: a message sealed today and opened at five, ten, thirteen, eighteen, on leaving home, or whenever the child chooses. Sealed with the same provenance ledger as the film, so what opens is exactly what was written or recorded. Sensitive messages are never machine-triggered; the parent chooses the key. The parent's side shows 'sealed' and never a count.
tasks.note: src/anuvritti/adapters/persistence/inbox.py is declared out of service: the Future Inbox store is built and the container does not hold it.

tasks.description: Papa Today: the home screen occasionally taps you on the shoulder. 'Leave him a twenty-second message.' 'Put the phone down and go sit with her.' 'You once saved something about the moon. Look outside tonight.' At most one line a day, drawn from the archive, sometimes telling the parent to close the app. Never counted, never streaked, and a whole month of silence is a valid output.

The Return, with ceremony: the one suggestion arrives (duration.arrive) onto the ground with the reason set in the display face above it, the rest of the vault quiet until it is answered. The Spark's reverse gets a waveform, so a why is spoken by turning the object over: release, upload, POST /sparks/{id}/why, and the back re-renders in saffron with the player. An empty back stays a finished state; no call to action in indigo.

Promise/Kept: when a Moment's Spark carries a why recording, the film emits one scene playing the why from capture and then the trace from 'Did this happen?', in that order, with the real gap between them spoken as language. A scene of this kind cannot hold a synthetic voice, and the compiler refuses any bridge between the two recordings.

The Annual Interview, in two voices: on each birthday the same short questions to the child ('What is Papa terrible at?') and to the parent, recorded, filed against the age, never re-recorded. The film gains a second narrator, and the film at eight plays the answers at four, five, six and seven. PRD 34 as written: the child's own voice, as a yearly artifact.

Ask Papa, later: a Right Now answer to 'What question did he ask that you could not answer?' becomes a TELL Spark with no date. The Return Engine hands it back once, years on, on age alone: 'She asked this when she was four.' The answer is a recording filed against the question, and the film gets 'Your questions, and what Papa found out'. Never listed as unanswered, never counted.

The Dictionary of Us: a WORD Little Thing, the child's invented word in the child's own voice with the day it was first heard. The film gets a chapter in first-heard order; the offline reader renders it as a glossary. Deliberately no 'does she still say it?' prompt, so it records arrivals and never losses.

Sealed capsules: an Age N capsule (letters, a grandparent's message, the year's film) sealed until the birthday; and The Unfinished, addressed to the child at an age the parent chooses, compiled only from Sparks with a recorded why and no Moment, narrated only by those whys. The parent sees 'sealed' and never a list, so the unlived is a gift to the child and never a debt to the parent.

Let's Do Something: 'We have fifteen minutes. Rainy day.' A curated, versioned set of offline activities, terrible jokes and bedtime ideas that ends every time with 'Phone goes away now.' The only screen whose success is the app closing. Content lives in the repository as data with an author and a date, and a constitution test forbids any activity that keeps a child on a screen.

Return signals beyond age and weekend: season, a birthday within the month, the child's stated interests from Right Now, and a parent-approved event. Each signal is a pure scorer with a name, and no signal may raise urgency, only fit. 'Look outside tonight' becomes possible.
Lift the V0 gate: COOK, VISIT, TELL and LISTEN join the intents, so a recipe, a place, a story to tell and a song each have a home. The spoken engine learns their first-person shapes.

Right Now returns to its own cadence: every few months, two minutes, several fields at once, as PRD 17 wrote it. The daily single question becomes an occasional snapshot, because a daily question is the shape of a habit and the anti-metrics exist to refuse habits.

What the child sees: one screen, one real recording, then it ends. Wind Down plays a parent's goodnight and stops; the Sound Garden plays one sound and says 'Roar with me', then the screen goes dark on its own. No navigation, no library, no autoplay, nothing to tap twice. The first child-facing surface, and the first test that a screen ends itself.

tasks.description: Persist a Future Inbox seal atomically through repository and media ports: encrypt the private artifact at rest and commit its portable provenance ledger with it, with crash-recovery tests proving neither can exist alone.

tasks.role: Senior Staff Backend Engineer / Security Engineer
tasks.description: Authenticate each portable Future Inbox ledger offline with the family-held film authenticity key, so replacement of both an artifact and its digest is distinguishable years later without the archive or a network.

tasks.role: Senior Staff Backend Engineer / Security Engineer
tasks.description: Give the family authenticity key a recoverable, versioned ceremony: encrypted second-copy backup, rehearsed recovery and rotation, and a content-free inventory showing which film and Future Inbox anchors each key version covers.

Email-in ingest, so a grandparent can contribute with nothing installed and nothing learned. The mailbox is read at the interface layer (a drop folder or an inbound webhook); tests/constitution/test_no_public_model.py forbids imaplib/smtplib under adapters/, and that stays.

Search across the family archive that answers in the family's own words: SQLite FTS5 over captions, whys and transcripts, with FamilyLexicon synonyms. Embeddings (sqlite-vec + a small ONNX model via onnxruntime, never transformers) only if the month proves keyword search poor.
Constellations: categories emerge from what a family actually saves and name themselves in the family's own words, instead of a taxonomy the parent must learn.

phases.name: Phase 9: Real - a server, a backup, a phone, a month

tasks.description: A backup that has been restored: scheduled `sqlite3 .backup` plus media to an off-site copy, the Fernet key escrowed where a second person can find it, and a restore performed into a scratch container. Ten lines in docs/CONTINUITY.md say where the key is, where the backup is, and how to restore.

Choose durable family render-receipt key custody: define recovery, rotation, multi-device access and loss semantics, and connect them to the rehearsed family backup and restore design before receipt anchors become automatic.
Schema migration with a forward path and a rehearsed way back, applied against a copy of a real archive before it is applied to one.
tasks.note: src/anuvritti/adapters/persistence/migrations.py is declared out of service: the container calls schema.migrate(), so the rehearse-before-apply engine never runs.

tasks.description: A server that is not the laptop: the existing image on one small box behind Caddy for TLS (or Tailscale Serve for one family), a deploy workflow that pushes the image, `public_url` and trusted-proxy settings, and a liveness ping the backup cron sends. `curl https://host/ready` shows encryption at rest on.

The app on the founder's phone: eas.json with an internal-distribution profile, the server URL baked in, the App Group and share-extension profiles provisioned, an install link tapped on a real iPhone and a real Android. docs/DEVICE.md executed and dated. Closes TASK-513 honestly.
tasks.note: NOT RUN. docs/DEVICE.md says so at the top: the five things it lists - the share sheet, the flip, the keychain across a cold start, ten seconds measured, the microphone - all need hardware, and no hardware has run them.

tasks.description: A privacy budget for logs: no content, no transcript, no filename and no child's name can reach a log line, asserted by reading the emitted stream back.
tasks.note: src/anuvritti/application/import_.py is declared out of service: the importer has no CLI and no route.

tasks.description: Crash-free capture: a process killed mid-write loses nothing, because the spool journals before it acts and replays on launch.
tasks.note: src/widgets/right-now-widget.ts is declared out of service: no native widget extension consumes it.

tasks.description: The return arrives on the lock screen: local notifications scheduled on device, at most one a day, silenceable forever in one tap and never re-enabled by an update.
tasks.note: src/return/notifications.ts is declared out of service: no screen registers the scheduler.

tasks.description: Import what already exists: a Photos export, a WhatsApp chat, a Notes dump become Sparks and Moments with source IMPORTED and their original dates, so the first film has a childhood in it and not a month. Nothing is inferred that the import did not carry.

ADR-0006, the tenant is the process: one container and one SQLite file per family, which is what ADR-0003 already means. Supersedes the many-families-one-server assumption under TASK-901, 1105, 1112 and 1211; 1211 is closed by it. Auth becomes 'who may pair with this box'.

Thirty days, for real: PRD 54 run on the founder's own phone against the real server, the year's film compiled at the end of it, and the dated answer written in docs/VALIDATION.md: did Anuvritti create one moment that would not have happened otherwise? This is the gate on Phases 10 to 14, and the answer is allowed to be no.
tasks.note: NOT RUN. docs/VALIDATION.md says so at the top. Thirty days with one real family, then a document written from it; the previous close was a document written from tests/e2e fixtures.

tasks.description: Co-parent: a second adult with equal standing, not a guest account.

Grandparent: one prompt, one tap, from a link, nothing installed. Thirty days before the child turns N the grandparent receives exactly one question keyed to N - 'What was his father like at N?' - and the recording is filed against two ages at once. Skippable forever; never re-asked.
Child data rights: the child can hide what they choose now and own the whole record later.
Real authentication and enforced family isolation - HARDENING 5.1 closed completely, which is the gate on any second family existing.

tasks.description: A restore that runs on a schedule into a scratch environment and proves the archive is readable, because a backup nobody has restored is a rumour.
Ten years of one family loaded and the archive still answers in the time a parent will wait: a soak test against a full archive, not an empty one.
Compilation as a durable job: submitted, resumable, and idempotent on the hash of the spec, so a retry is never a second film.
Determinism proven by hash: the same spec and the same bytes produce the same film, this year and in ten years.
tasks.note: Byte-identical frames will not survive a Chromium upgrade; TASK-1208's perceptual diff is the real gate. Scope this to spec + timeline hashes, not pixels.

tasks.description: The render worker runs with no network, a read-only root and the family's media mounted for one job only, then removed.
Progress in words a parent reads and a cancel that actually stops the machine, rather than a bar that lies until it finishes.
A ceiling on time and cost, checked before the first frame: a film that would take an hour is refused up front with a sentence, not discovered half-rendered.
Failure that tells a family something true: a dead letter carries the scene, the citation and the human sentence, and never a stack trace to a parent.
Artifact lifecycle: the rendered film expires from the render host on a clock, and never from the family's own archive.
Golden frames: a perceptual diff over a fixed set of scenes, so a token change can never quietly redraw a film a family has already seen.
Captions and an audio description on every film by default, because the grandmother who cannot hear it is exactly who it was made for.
The Sound Garden as a licence-clean audio bed whose provenance is recorded exactly like everything else the film claims.
tasks.note: PRD 30 'Sound Garden' is a child sound-play surface (TASK-818); this is the film's audio bed.

tasks.description: Backpressure and fairness: one family compiling eighteen years cannot make another family wait for five seconds of their child's voice.
tasks.note: Closed by ADR-0006 (TASK-909) if the tenant is the process.

tasks.description: The compiler's constitution runs where the film is made: the render worker boots with --network none and compiles, verifies and renders a real archive end to end. Anything that needs the network fails out loud. This is the runtime twin of the static import walk.
The archive format written down as a specification: versioned, human-readable, and complete enough that someone could write a reader from it alone.
One command produces the whole archive as ordinary files a person can open in twenty years with nothing of ours installed.
Forward compatibility against a corpus: every archive version ever shipped is opened by today's reader, in a test that grows with each release.
A filmspec from an older version compiles on today's compiler or is refused out loud - it is never drawn differently in silence.
The time-travel test: an archive captured now, compiled against a clock set eighteen years forward, and still correct in every date it says out loud.
What happens if we stop existing: keys escrowed to the family, the format published, and the reader already in their hands - written as a procedure, not a promise.
The offline reader: one HTML file that opens an exported archive with no server, no account and no network, and looks like Anuvritti because it uses the same tokens.
The year as an object you can hold: a print-ready artifact generated from the same spec that makes the film.
The Family Artifact Protocol made real: a signed, self-describing bundle a family can hand to another generation.
Link rot answered: what was saved from the internet is kept as content with its own provenance, because a URL is not a memory.
Fixity over decades: a scheduled check that re-hashes the whole archive, and a repair path for the day one file comes back wrong.
Eighteen simulated years: captured, compiled, exported and reopened by the offline reader in one test that stands for the whole promise.

phases.name: Phase 14: A Product a Family Can Have
phases.owner: Design Lead / Senior Staff Backend Engineer

tasks.description: First run under sixty seconds that ends in a saved Spark rather than a tour, because the product explains itself by working.
The invitation: a co-parent or grandparent joins by receiving something worth having, not by being asked to create an account first.
Entitlements where nothing already saved is ever held hostage: if a family stops paying, the archive stays readable and exportable forever.
The gift path: a grandparent can pay for the legacy archive without becoming the owner of the child's record.
Measurement that cannot become surveillance: counted on the device, reported family-blind, and never able to name a child or a moment.
The anti-metrics enforced in code: no streak, no daily active target, no session length goal - a test that fails if one is ever introduced.
Messages that cannot nag: a hard ceiling, a permanent off switch, and no copy that exists to bring somebody back.
The trust page, written for a parent and not a lawyer: what is stored, where, who can read it, and what happens to it if we disappear.
A way to reach a person, and a support path that cannot read the family's archive to help them.
Incident response rehearsed rather than written: a drill that produces the notification a family would actually receive, within the hours we claim.
The published terms tested against the code: every promise the privacy policy makes has an assertion behind it, and a broken promise fails the build.
The product's most important test, run against the real build: would a parent be glad, in fifteen years, that this existed.
